title: Pippa and the Splashy Stream
markdown:
Pippa the pony, with her mane the colour of a sunrise — a dazzling pink, mind you! — was as cheerful as a bumblebee in a field of clover. Every happy step she took made her mane bounce and sway. And who was her trusty co-adventurer? Nutmeg the dormouse! This little fellow, with eyes like shiny brown marbles, was perched on a smooth grey stone that had cleverly hitched a ride on Pippa’s back. Tucked safely in a tiny woven basket beside him, filled to the very brim, was the most delicious wildflower honey you ever did smell.

“This honey,” chirped Nutmeg, his voice as light as dandelion fluff, “is absolutely extraordinary! It’s from the very finest wildflowers, gathered with the most patient care and a whisper of moonlight.”

Pippa nodded, her nose twitching. “And it’s for the Wrigglebottom family! They’re having their annual Blossom Festival today. Oh, Nutmeg, I do hope they’ll think it’s just as special as we do! The festival starts promptly at noon, and the best honey is always served first!”

Delivering treats and bringing smiles was Pippa’s very favourite kind of mission. It made her feel like a true hero of happiness. But as they trotted along the sun-dappled path, a tiny ticklish flutter began to stir in her tummy. Just ahead, glinting merrily in the sunshine, was the Whispering Stream. It wasn’t a roaring river. It was quite small, no wider than three of Pippa’s sturdy hoof-prints, but it was new. Pippa had never, ever crossed it before.

“Oh, Nutmeg,” she whispered, her happy trot slowing. “Look. The stream. It looks terribly splashy.”

Her hooves, usually so light and ready for a gallop, felt suddenly very heavy. The butterfly in her tummy did a rather dramatic somersault.

Nutmeg, whose sharp eyes missed nothing, tilted his little head. “Splashy, you say? Yes! It sings a joyful song when the water dances over the smooth stones. But don’t you worry your lovely pink mane, Pippa! Remember those sunbeams we chased yesterday? You weren’t worried about them one bit!”

“Sunbeams don’t splash you right on your nose,” Pippa mumbled, ears drooping just a tiny bit. The precious basket of honey seemed to grow heavier with every hesitant step.

They reached the very edge of the stream. The water chuckled and gurgled, a playful bubbly sound that bounced off the pebbles. Pippa saw her reflection, and oh dear, it was a wobbly pony looking quite uncertain. She imagined her hooves slipping on a wet stone, and her heart gave a little thump.

Nutmeg’s whiskers twitched. “Sometimes the best way across isn’t the most obvious way! Turning back might seem easy, Pippa, but then the Wrigglebottoms won’t get their honey in time!”

He scurried from his stone-seat onto Pippa’s back, tiny paws tapping near her ear. “Look! Do you see them? The big, smooth stones! They make a perfect path. They don’t wiggle or wobble. They just sit there, solid as a freshly baked biscuit!”

Pippa looked. And she saw! Several large flat stones, placed just so, like stepping-stones, forming a clear dry path right across the water. They looked wonderfully steady, like little islands waiting patiently.

“But… but what if I step on one and it wobbles anyway?” Her voice was still a little shaky.

Nutmeg, brave as a very, very tiny lion, hopped onto the very first stone. He stood there, testing it with all his might. It didn’t budge an inch. “This stone is as steady as a sleeping hedgehog! And that one,” he pointed, “is as sturdy as a sturdy oak leaf!”

Pippa took a deep, deep breath. The air smelled of wildflowers and warm friendly earth. Meadowlarks chirped high above. It wasn’t a scary dark place. It was just a stream. And she had a very important delivery to make.

“Alright,” she said, gaining a little more confidence. “I’ll try. But you keep talking, Nutmeg. Like a very encouraging weather report!”

Nutmeg giggled, tiny bells. “Will do! The forecast for Pippa’s bravery is… sunny with a chance of enormous, spectacular courage!”

With Nutmeg cheering from the first solid stone, Pippa carefully, deliberately, stepped onto the second. The stone felt rough and cool beneath her hoof. It held her weight steady. Oh! It doesn’t wobble at all! It’s like walking on the meadow floor! She took another step, and then another. The water splashed gently around the stones, making little rainbow-coloured droplets, but it didn’t splash her.

Then came the last stone. It was a little farther away, and as Pippa gathered herself to jump, the water surged and splashed around it, a rainbow mist rising. She felt the spray cool on her nose, heard the gurgling, smelled the damp earth mixing with sweet flower scents. Her heart thumped like a drum. To keep the precious honey safe, she stretched her neck further than she liked, her pink mane catching the breeze. She willingly got a little splash on her nose.

And then, quite suddenly, she was on the other side! The meadow stretched out, a carpet of green and gold, and there, not far away, were the familiar cozy burrows of the Wrigglebottom family. Sweet relief, then a burst of pure joy. Her tummy butterfly was no longer doing worried flips. It was soaring!

“We did it!” Pippa whinnied, a happy sound that echoed through the meadow.

Mr. and Mrs. Wrigglebottom, along with their littlest bunnies, all with twitching noses and bright eyes, hopped out to greet them. “Pippa! Nutmeg! You’re here! And what a glorious basket of honey you’ve brought!” exclaimed Mrs. Wrigglebottom.

As Pippa watched the bunnies dip their tiny spoons into the golden honey, their faces beaming, a warm contented glow spread all through her.

Later, as they trotted home, the sun casting long friendly shadows that stretched like sleepy cats, a small puddle sparkled on the path. Pippa trotted right through it, sending a joyful spray dancing in the air. The Whispering Stream still gurgled and chuckled, but now it sounded like a happy secret being shared.

“That was quite an adventure, wasn’t it, Pippa?” Nutmeg said, snuggled on his stone-seat.

Pippa nudged him gently with her soft nose. “It was. And you know what? The stream wasn’t so splashy after all. It was just a stream. And I am Pippa the pony who crossed it!”

Her bright pink mane seemed to shimmer with an extra sparkle in the fading sunlight. One drop of stream-water still sat on her nose, and she did not shake it off until they were home.
